gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-georgia: Noto Sans Georgian opens its curves wide and trims its ascender stems short, so the lowercase body looks generous. The stretched, unshaded outline of Nulshock is the quality that stands out most.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-glagoli: Nulshock stretches wide, bold and technical, with spacing to spare. It excels at striking, uniform outlines up top, while Noto Sans Glagolitic does its best work staying clear in small sizes.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-grantha: Nulshock draws each stroke at a single measured thickness, then stretches the letters out with generous spacing. Noto Sans Grantha, in turn, is built for smooth reading, its flattened bowls never snagging the eye.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-gunjala: Wide and bold: Nulshock keeps its line constant through every turn. Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi brings modern, crayon-thick lowercase strokes, with terminals cut back to leave a big gap.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-hebrew: Technical is the word for Nulshock, stretched and spaced out. Nulshock is at its best in blunt, uniform outlines, while Noto Sans Hebrew excels with a dominant midsection and generous gaps at curve ends.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-imperia: Approachable describes Noto Sans Imperial Aramaic, its c ends pointing apart like pincers. Against the uniform, glare-free lines of Nulshock, a full page of text would glide along, capitals barely rising above the lowercase.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-jp: Nulshock draws plain, unshaded constant-width lines, stretched wide with spacious tracking and a bold, technical stance throughout. Noto Sans JP flows on easily, its lofty lowercase and sweeping curves open.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-kannada: Nulshock stretches out in bold, monoline strokes throughout, spaced generously and unmistakably technical. And Noto Sans Kannada reads gently across a full page, with s curves opening wide at both ends.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-kayah-l: Brush ends lift away before each curve closes, a light touch beside the marker-tip lines of Nulshock. Noto Sans Kayah Li carries text smoothly, with capitals only slightly taller than the lowercase.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-limbu: Contemporary best describes Noto Sans Limbu, whose curves gape wide. Most striking is Nulshock, stretched and bold, whose stroke weight never varies, set against a lowercase that fills out its line.
